prompt: Complete two reviewer-owned unfamiliar technical-documentation exercises at materially different urgency and system scale. After the first defense, the reviewer changes at least one audience/decision, one evidence-confidence assumption, and one safety, lifecycle or communication constraint. Produce independent evidence without published model answers, employer-confidential material or production authority.

Canonical claim ledger with stable identities classes sources windows units confidence sensitivity owners and unknowns

evidenceRequirements: Use reviewer-owned fictional or sanitized disposable content only
No employer incident customer record credential token vulnerability private endpoint contract or confidential communication
Every material claim distinguishes observation calculation decision declaration inference and unknown
Every source records identity version observation window and access or review date where relevant
Every timestamp has an explicit offset and normalized chronology preserves original evidence
Every diagram answers a named question and has a meaning-equivalent text alternative
Every mutating procedure step binds exact target authority prediction validation abort and recovery
Normative language is used only with a named policy or specification authority
Accepted decisions are superseded by new linked records rather than rewritten
Incident communication does not promote hypotheses to facts or leak sensitive implementation detail
Post-incident analysis explains system conditions and verifies action effectiveness rather than assigning individual blame
Audience views preserve canonical facts while changing emphasis and allowed detail
Automated checks are not presented as factual human or operational acceptance
Reviewer controls hidden changes scoring follow-up defense rehearsal and cleanup proof
